Response: This section has been revised and the sentence as quoted is no longer used.
<u>Comment</u>: Washington points out that "...resolving of problems encountered by endangered species must not be based solely upon protection of that species."
Response: This is a reservation raised repeatedly by other States, and we agree with the statement. But it should be recognized that specific management measures cannot and should not be legislated. Only a carefully planned, yet flexible, program of management can effectively restore a species.

This management must include appropriate protection. Protective measures can be legislated to a degree and this is why the proposed action appears to advocate protection at the omission of other forms of management. An appropriate balance between protection of the species and management of other components of its ecosystem will be reflected in recovery plans for each species and subspecies prepared within the authority of the proposed Act.
